stem: Qasim shades a unit square. He takes $\frac{1}{2}$ of the square and then $\frac{1}{5}$ of that half to show $\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{5}$.

parts.text: Which claim correctly reads the shaded product?

options.text: The product is the label rectangle area, with no link to the shaded fraction.
The shaded piece is $\frac{1}{10}$ of the unit square, and that area equals $\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{5}$.
Shade $\frac{1}{2}$ of the square and stop; the product needs no further share of that half.
The same shading finds the perimeter of the unit square.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: One fifth of one half of the unit square is one tenth of the unit square, so the shaded area equals the product $\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{5}$.

teacher.key_rationale: Half of the unit square, then one fifth of that half, is 1/10 of the unit square and equals the product. Stopping at a label, omitting the second factor, or reading perimeter all miss the area model.
